title: Lymph node and soft tissue ultrasound
what: The doctor uses ultrasound to look at the lymph nodes, the skin, and the tissue under the skin. It is safe and uses no radiation.
why: When a lymph node is swollen, there is a lump or hard spot under the skin, after an injury, or to keep watch on a growth.
tell_doctor: Where and when you noticed the lump or node
If you recently had a cold, sore throat, or a vaccine
If you have had surgery in this area

prepare.title: Preparation
prepare.text: No special preparation is needed. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Wear clothes that make it easy to uncover the area: your neck, armpits, or groin.

bring: Past ultrasound reports, if you have them
A tissue or towel to wipe off the gel
steps: You lie down or sit and uncover the area
The doctor puts on cool gel
The probe is moved over the skin above the node or lump
Sometimes the same area on the other side is checked for comparison
feel: The probe presses a little. It does not hurt
after: The gel is wiped off, and you can go back to your usual day right away
You usually get the report right away
Sometimes the doctor advises a repeat scan later, or a biopsy. This means taking a few cells with a thin needle

faq.q: Is a swollen lymph node dangerous?
faq.a: Most often, nodes swell because of a cold or inflammation, and they shrink on their own. Ultrasound helps the doctor decide if anything else is needed.

faq.q: Do I need to prepare for a lymph node ultrasound?
faq.a: No. You can eat and drink as usual.
